*Āsavavippayuttasāsavaduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 15.36) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the Paṭṭhāna collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka. The text constitutes a leaf section structured around the dyad of states dissociated from, yet subject to, defilements or pollutants (*āsavavippayuttasāsavaduka*) considered in conjunction with the triad of wholesome states (*kusalattika*).

No cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora are recorded [DharmaNexus]. However, automated text analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse across the Abhidhamma, comprising 157 matching passages shared with 48 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest textual overlaps are found in closely related Paṭṭhāna sections, including *Āsavagocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.4; 14 matches, 3,214 characters), *Kusalattika, Āsavaparāmāsagocchaka* (Patthana 4.4; 13 matches, 2,869 characters), and a parallel treatment in *Āsavavippayuttasāsavaduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 21.11; 3 matches, 1,584 characters, exhibiting 0.85 similarity between segments §0.3–4.1_2 and §0.3–3.1_2) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits significant phraseological reuse with adjacent dyadic treatments, such as *Āsavasampayuttaduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 15.34) and *Āsavavippayuttasāsavaduka, Sanidassanattika* (Patthana 21.50) [DharmaNexus].
